pages.text: "Just one more cookie!" Coco quietly took a cookie from the shop shelf and ate it. The third already. Mom called from the kitchen, "Apple pie for dinner today! Until then, just one cookie."
"Apple pie! I'll eat a whole pie at dinner!" Coco hopped with joy. But every time Coco passed the shelf, another cookie, and another. "Just a little more..." The cookie plate was empty.
It was dinner time. A steaming apple pie came to the table. But Coco's tummy was swollen and ached a little. "Ooh, I'm full... I can't eat pie." Coco's mouth drooped.

Mom gently rubbed Coco's tummy. "The cookies filled you up. There's no room for pie." Mrs. Magpie, who saw everything from the roof, sat on the windowsill. "Five cookies. I saw them all." Coco sank onto the stool.
Mom whispered, "Your tummy is a little bread basket. Fill it with cookies, and the pie won't fit." A basket full of cookies had no room for even one slice of pie. "Oh! I need to leave some space!"
Mom put a little plate beside the dinner bowl, with just one cookie on it. "Starting tomorrow, this is your plate. Just one cookie—dinner first!" Coco stared at the single cookie.
The next day, Coco passed the shelf. Their paw crept toward the cookies... Coco held it tightly closed and waited. "Just one cookie—dinner first!" Mrs. Magpie nodded from the windowsill.

At dinner, Coco's tummy gave a little rumble. Coco ate the apple pie. Yum, yum! It was delicious. "Wow! Was pie always this tasty?" Coco's tail swished happily. One cookie waited on the plate beside them.
Now Coco knew every word. "One, just one cookie! Two, dinner first! Three, finish dinner, then have the cookie!" The cookie plate on the shelf stayed full until dinner.
Mom lifted Coco into her arms. "It was hard to wait for the cookie, wasn't it?" Fewer cookies make dinner taste better. Coco nibbled the one cookie. "Just one cookie—dinner first!"
